item.title: Jensen Huang pulls out of ElevenLabs Summit amid Nvidia controversy
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: The Nvidia CEO also pulled out of an Anthropic event earlier.

item.title: YouTube streaming data returns to Billboard charts, ending major disagreement
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: YouTube will resume sharing streaming data with Billboard in 2027 after changes to the chart formula give more weight to free, ad-supported music streams.

item.title: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: Anthropic says the new models "show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision," as well as in communicating more clearly with users.

item.title: AI hardware startup Nominal triples valuation to $3B in 8 months
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Nominal, a startup that offers an AI platform for hardware engineering and claims Anduril as a major customer, has raised another big round of financing that triples its valuation.

item.title: France blames Iran for mass-hacks targeting freezers in grocery stores and blood banks
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: France's foreign minister blamed Iran for launching at least two waves of cyberattacks targeting industrial refrigerated and freezer units across France and wider Europe.

item.title: Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy puts Nvidia’s China ambitions under scrutiny
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy threatens to complicate Nvidia’s lobbying efforts to loosen U.S. chip export restrictions and maintain access to China’s lucrative AI market.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, a new lightweight model for agent execution
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: At 10 cents per million input tokens, Ember is significantly cheaper than frontier competitors like Haiku and Luna.

item.title: Uber launches parking service following SpotHero acquisition, with an eye on robotaxis
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Uber Parking is the latest example of the company offering products beyond its core ride-hailing service.

item.title: Anthropic joins AI’s natural gas frenzy, buys $3.4B worth of turbines
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Anthropic bought billions of dollars' worth of natural gas turbines in a deal that could give it buyer's remorse.

item.title: Medium’s new TK app brings AI assistance directly into the writing process
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Medium's new writing app embraces AI-assisted writing, despite growing controversy over the technology's role in publishing.

item.title: Meta expands Instagram’s AI age-guessing tech globally
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: Meta says it will use its AI technology to look for clues about people it suspects to be teenagers — even if they use an adult birthday.

item.title: Waymo robotaxis kept illegally passing school buses after software fix, feds say
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: The update to Waymo's self-driving system was rolled out nearly a year ago.

item.title: Meet Drops, the new music app bringing back the fun of sharing songs with friends
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: The new music discovery app lets users scroll through 10- to 30-second snippets of songs, comment, and share with friends.

item.title: Automattic debuts a platform to deploy vibe-coding apps amid a changing internet
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Automattic aims to compete with the likes of Lovable with Spacefast.

item.title: Musk says Tesla will refund some Cybertruck deposits, defends decision to end production
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Elon Musk defended the company's decision to stop making the Cybertruck, which will go out of production in around eight months.

item.title: Tesla expands robotaxi service to San Antonio
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: This will be the next Texas city in which Tesla will launch robotaxis.

item.title: Is Jensen Huang’s job on the line? Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld estimates it’s ‘about a 50-50’
item.dc:creator: Connie Loizos
item.description: Nvidia’s board is investigating Jensen Huang over his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld thinks it’s roughly a coin flip whether Huang stays on as CEO.

item.title: Apps to distract you from the endless cycle of doomscrolling

item.title: Nvidia will investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with possible Chinese spy

item.title: If Snap’s Specs are still ridiculously expensive, they’re also a lot more comfortable than they used to be
